content.content:
1	Many liquid handling installations add a small, accurately measured quantity of a concentrate to a much larger stream of a carrier liquid that is already flowing in a pipe. The concentrate may be aggressive, staining, strongly coloured, biologically active, or simply expensive, and the quantity that must be added is small in comparison with the carrier flow. The addition therefore has to be made repeatably, without measuring the concentrate by eye, and without allowing the concentrate to reach any part of the installation other than the carrier stream itself.
2	
3	Two practical difficulties dominate this kind of dosing. The first is separation of the two liquids upstream of the point of addition. A dosing device sits between a concentrate source and a pressurised carrier line, and any path that momentarily connects the two allows carrier liquid to be forced back into the concentrate source or allows concentrate to migrate into the carrier line at a time when no dose is called for. Devices that rely on separately actuated shut-off elements to keep the two sides apart depend on those elements being commanded in the correct order, so a control fault, a lost signal, or a slow-acting element can open both sides at once.
4	
5	The second difficulty is residue. The surfaces that the concentrate touches, in particular the port through which it enters the metering volume and the seat of the check element through which the dose leaves, retain a film of concentrate after the dose has been delivered. That film drips into the carrier stream between doses, so the quantity actually added is not the quantity that was measured. It also dries, crystallises, or reacts on the wetted surfaces, so that a valve which was accurate when new drifts, sticks, or seizes in service. The usual remedy is to break the valve out of the line and clean it by hand, which takes the installation out of service and exposes the person doing the work to the concentrate. Where a rinse is provided at all, it is commonly a separate operation that has to be commanded after the dose, and it therefore depends on an operator or a controller performing an extra step at the right moment.
6	
7	Dose selection presents a further difficulty. Adjustable dosing devices are often set by a screw or by an electronically stored value. A screw setting can be lost during cleaning and gives no indication of what was set. An electronic setting requires power, a sensor and a display at the valve, which is unwelcome in wet, washdown or hazardous locations, and it tells the operator only what the controller believes rather than what the mechanism will actually deliver.
8	
9	There remains a need for an inline metering valve in which the separation of the concentrate from the carrier liquid is enforced by the geometry of the moving parts rather than by the order in which external commands arrive, in which the surfaces wetted by the concentrate are rinsed by the carrier liquid as an unavoidable part of the return of the metering element, and in which the selected dose is both retained and displayed mechanically.
10

1	In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.
2	
3	FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.
4	
5	The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the only liquid used to rinse the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.
6	
7	FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.
8	
9	The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.
10	
11	A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall and so forms an annular space that travels with the piston 28. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke by an external actuating member, whether a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction. The one-way outlet valve 38 may take any form that passes liquid in one direction only, such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element.
12	
13	In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20, where it occupies the annular space at the waist 34 and forms a measured volume of concentrate. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.
14	
15	Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.
16	
17	The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.
18	
19	FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting indicia 54.
20	
21	The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.
22	
23	The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting, so that the index collar 40 is held against vibration and against the forces transmitted through the follower pin 44 until it is next indexed.
24	
25	The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting indicia 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting indicium presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics, without power at the valve and without a controller. In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.

FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.

The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the only liquid used to rinse the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.

FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall and so forms an annular space that travels with the piston 28. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke by an external actuating member, whether a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction. The one-way outlet valve 38 may take any form that passes liquid in one direction only, such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20, where it occupies the annular space at the waist 34 and forms a measured volume of concentrate. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.

The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting indicia 54.

The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting, so that the index collar 40 is held against vibration and against the forces transmitted through the follower pin 44 until it is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting indicia 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting indicium presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics, without power at the valve and without a controller. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the mechanism itself rather than a stored value, so the displayed setting cannot disagree with the volume that the valve will deliver.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and a flush bypass 26.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20 and carries the film of concentrate remaining on that wall ahead of it, so that the rinse which follows is presented with a wetted surface rather than with standing liquid.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38. Those are the two surfaces on which concentrate is otherwise retained after a dose, the first because concentrate stands in the mouth of the port and the second because concentrate is the last liquid to pass the seat.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore leaves by the same route as the dose and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26, so that carrier liquid at the pressure of the main line is never presented to an open concentrate port 22 and cannot be driven back toward the concentrate source. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped, so that it removes a film with clean carrier liquid instead of diluting a standing charge of concentrate.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the wearing and sealing parts are replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line. The parts that contact the concentrate are the parts that are exchanged, so a change of concentrate or a worn sealing land is dealt with by fitting a further cartridge rather than by dismantling the installation.

The materials of the metering sleeve 18, the piston 28, the flexible lip 56 and the sealing elements are selected for compatibility with the carrier liquid and with the concentrate to be dosed. The spring-biased detent 48 may be a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger, and the flexible lip 56 may be formed integrally with the upstream sealing land 30 or as a separate resilient element retained on it.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The travel of the piston 28 on this stroke is limited by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46, which sets the measured volume.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting indicium then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. The valve is thereby left charged, rinsed and set, ready for the following cycle.

The foregoing description sets out embodiments of the invention. A skilled reader may make changes of detail to the described embodiments without departing from the scope of the claims that follow.

content.text: I've read all inputs, the ten draft sections, the numerals table, and all four figure briefs. Here is the complete ledger review.

input.summary:
Source authority is a single USER passage, reproduced identically in input/disclosure.md and the one USER turn of input/conversation.md. input/brief.md supplies only title, applicant/inventor, "Not applicable." for cross-reference and government support, claim classes, and the preserved terminology list (metering sleeve, dose chamber, flush bypass, index collar, flush poppet, annular rinse channel) — all of which the draft honors.

LEDGER — SUPPORTED. The great majority of the application traces cleanly. Every limitation of independent claims 1 and 13 traces to the disclosure ("The valve has a cylindrical housing with an inlet at one axial end and an outlet at the opposite axial end"; "The sleeve defines a cylindrical dose chamber, a radial concentrate port, a carrier-liquid admission port, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber"; "two axially spaced sealing lands joined by a reduced-diameter waist"; "Movement to the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port"; "the follower pin opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"; "Carrier liquid flows through an annular rinse channel between the sleeve and housing, through two radial rinse openings ... and then through the flush bypass to the outlet"; "The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port"). Dependent claims 2–8, 10–12, 14–18 and 20 likewise trace (two directed rinse openings; flexible lip on the upstream land wiping first; port/land ordering; index collar with helical cam groove indexed one increment per full stroke; three axial stop faces setting three dose volumes; spring-biased detent in one of three recesses; cartridge contents and threaded end cap; cylindrical housing with end inlet/outlet). Claim 1's generalization from "two radial rinse openings" to "at least one rinse opening" is a permissible narrowing-to-genus of a disclosed species. All 28 numerals in numerals.md are used consistently, each denotes one part, and the numerals listed on each figure sheet match the numerals the detailed description attributes to that figure. No section line is named in any view, so there is no section-designation mismatch to report. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains. The Background is prior-art framing only and cites no reference.

LEDGER — UNTRACED (4 critical findings). Four passages of the detailed description assert matter with no affirmative USER support: (a) the actuating source for the piston rod ("a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion"); (b) the form of the one-way outlet valve ("may take any form ... such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element") — this is precisely the kind of "any form ... such as" broadening added to justify the renderer's ball-on-seat choice in FIGS. 2 and 3, and must be removed from the text rather than kept; (c) a materials-selection sentence (the disclosure says nothing about materials, and it introduces the undefined, unnumbered term "the sealing elements"); (d) structural variants of the spring-biased detent ("a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger") and of the flexible lip ("formed integrally ... or as a separate resilient element"). None of these appears anywhere in the inventor's words.

SCOPE. The disclosure says the window "shows one of three reference numerals carried on the collar." The draft renames these throughout to "dose setting indicia," a genus broader than the disclosed species, and carries the broadened term into claims 9 and 19. Reported as a major claim_scope finding with a text-only fix; the FIG. 4 plain-patch depiction may stand as a schematic convention once the text says "numerals."

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (5 findings). FIG. 3 has two flow-path defects. First, the flush poppet is placed at the closed left (supply) end of the annular rinse channel, not at the flush bypass, contradicting the description and claims 1 and 13 ("a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"); and its stem geometry is self-contradictory — the pin is "left of the inner wall," the stem's driven end is under the pin, the stem "runs leftward to a conical head," yet the head is said to sit at a seat in the transverse boss, which lies to the right of the pin. Second, FIG. 3 assigns the lower half and the upper half of one and the same annulus two different identities and two different flows ("The clear gap between the lower bands is the annular rinse channel ... The gap between the upper bands is an open passage carrying liquid to the right"), and then has the flush bypass discharge into that same annulus, so the rinse stream recirculates instead of reaching the outlet. FIG. 4 is described in 07-drawings.md as having "a portion of the housing wall broken away," but the FIG. 4 brief contains no housing wall and no break line; it instead floats an unnumbered bracket that "does not touch the collar." FIG. 4 also spaces the three detent recesses along the collar's upper silhouette and the three indicia along the visible surface — i.e., axially — although both sets are selected by rotation of the collar, so an axially spaced set cannot be indexed by "one increment" of turn and cannot present one indicium at a time to the window. Two minor items: FIG. 1 renders the inlet and outlet as downward radial stubs on the same side of the housing, in tension with "an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end" (claim 12); and FIG. 2 omits the housing wall and annular gap that FIGS. 1 and 3 show over the same region, running the admission-port tube off-sheet as though carrier liquid were supplied externally rather than from inlet 14.

One further minor fidelity item: the description calls the carrier-liquid admission port "a radial port," a term the disclosure applies only to the concentrate port and the rinse openings.

Total: 12 findings — 4 critical, 5 major, 3 minor. Each carries a filing-clean fix that is text- or brief-side only; no fix adds a speculative shape or optional embodiment.

findings.title: Unsupported actuator variants for the piston rod
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "A piston 28 is axially slidable..." (sentence on piston rod 36)
findings.detail: The description asserts an external actuating member and names three alternative actuation sources. The disclosure never states how the piston is driven; it refers only to strokes of the piston and to the piston rod as the carrier of the follower pin. There is no affirmative USER passage naming a hand lever, a pneumatic actuator, a hydraulic actuator, or any other source of reciprocating motion.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke by an external actuating member, whether a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by a follower pin carried by the piston rod. Each full piston stroke turns the index collar by one increment." — the source names the rod and the stroke but no actuating member.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke."

findings.title: Unsupported "any form ... such as" broadening of the one-way outlet valve
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "A piston 28 is axially slidable..." (final sentence)
findings.detail: The description adds an open-ended genus and three species for the one-way outlet valve. The disclosure names the element only functionally. This sentence also operates as an application-text statement added to license the renderer's ball-on-conical-seat choice in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 briefs, which the preflight forbids: the depiction convention must stay confined to the figure brief and must not be justified by broadening the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The one-way outlet valve 38 may take any form that passes liquid in one direction only, such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve into the main flow." No affirmative passage describes any structure of that valve.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full. Leave the FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 briefs unchanged, since each already labels the ball and seat "shown schematically" and the claims and description remain shape-neutral as to the one-way outlet valve.

findings.title: Unsupported materials statement, and an undefined "sealing elements"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The materials of the metering sleeve 18..." (first sentence)
findings.detail: The description asserts a material-selection criterion. The disclosure contains no statement about materials, compatibility, or chemical resistance anywhere. The sentence also introduces "the sealing elements" as a part, with no numeral, no antecedent, and no source support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The materials of the metering sleeve 18, the piston 28, the flexible lip 56 and the sealing elements are selected for compatibility with the carrier liquid and with the concentrate to be dosed." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "The concentrate may be aggressive..." — this phrase does not appear in the disclosure at all; the disclosure's closest content is "A reusable inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable dose of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid," which says nothing about materials. No affirmative passage exists.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full.

findings.title: Unsupported structural variants of the spring-biased detent and the flexible lip
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The materials of the metering sleeve 18..." (second sentence)
findings.detail: The description offers a ball/plunger alternative for the detent and an integral/separate alternative for the flexible lip. The disclosure names both parts functionally only. Neither alternative is disclosed, and the detent alternative also serves to license the ball depicted in the FIG. 4 brief, which the preflight forbids the application text from doing.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The spring-biased detent 48 may be a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger, and the flexible lip 56 may be formed integrally with the upstream sealing land 30 or as a separate resilient element retained on it." Nearest sources (disclosure.md): "A spring-biased detent engages one of three recesses to retain the selected setting." and "a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land first wipes the dose-chamber wall." No affirmative passage describes the internal form of either part.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full (this removes the whole paragraph together with the preceding materials sentence). Leave the FIG. 4 detent depiction unchanged; it is already labeled "shown schematically" and, once this sentence is removed, the description and claims are shape-neutral as to the detent.

The draft substitutes the genus "indicia," which also reads on symbols, colours, bars or blank marks that the inventor never described, and carries that genus into two claims. No affirmative USER passage supports any non-numeral marking.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 9): "further comprising a transparent window in the housing and three dose setting indicia carried by the index collar"; candidate (claim 19): "displaying, through a transparent window in the housing, one of three dose setting indicia carried by the index collar". findings.title: FIG. 3 places the flush poppet at the closed supply end of the rinse channel, and its stem geometry is impossible

(1) The brief seats the poppet in a boss that closes the left end of the annular rinse channel — i.e. it gates the carrier-liquid supply — while the description and both independent claims recite a flush poppet connected to the flush bypass, which the same brief locates at the far right of the view. (2) The stem cannot reach the stated seat: the pin is left of the inner wall, hence left of the boss; the stem's driven end is under the pin; the stem then "runs leftward" to the head, placing the head further left still, yet the seat is said to be in the boss to the right.

The head stands clear of a seat in an opening through the transverse boss..." / "Right of that ball, a further opening through the upper inner band joins the bore to the upper passage: the flush bypass." structured_output.summary:
Source authority is a single USER passage, reproduced identically in input/disclosure.md and the one USER turn of input/conversation.md. input/brief.md supplies only title, applicant/inventor, "Not applicable." for cross-reference and government support, claim classes, and the preserved terminology list (metering sleeve, dose chamber, flush bypass, index collar, flush poppet, annular rinse channel) — all of which the draft honors.

LEDGER — SUPPORTED. The great majority of the application traces cleanly. Every limitation of independent claims 1 and 13 traces to the disclosure ("The valve has a cylindrical housing with an inlet at one axial end and an outlet at the opposite axial end"; "The sleeve defines a cylindrical dose chamber, a radial concentrate port, a carrier-liquid admission port, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber"; "two axially spaced sealing lands joined by a reduced-diameter waist"; "Movement to the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port"; "the follower pin opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"; "Carrier liquid flows through an annular rinse channel between the sleeve and housing, through two radial rinse openings ... and then through the flush bypass to the outlet"; "The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port"). Dependent claims 2–8, 10–12, 14–18 and 20 likewise trace (two directed rinse openings; flexible lip on the upstream land wiping first; port/land ordering; index collar with helical cam groove indexed one increment per full stroke; three axial stop faces setting three dose volumes; spring-biased detent in one of three recesses; cartridge contents and threaded end cap; cylindrical housing with end inlet/outlet). Claim 1's generalization from "two radial rinse openings" to "at least one rinse opening" is a permissible narrowing-to-genus of a disclosed species. All 28 numerals in numerals.md are used consistently, each denotes one part, and the numerals listed on each figure sheet match the numerals the detailed description attributes to that figure. No section line is named in any view, so there is no section-designation mismatch to report. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains. The Background is prior-art framing only and cites no reference.

LEDGER — UNTRACED (4 critical findings). Four passages of the detailed description assert matter with no affirmative USER support: (a) the actuating source for the piston rod ("a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion"); (b) the form of the one-way outlet valve ("may take any form ... such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element") — this is precisely the kind of "any form ... such as" broadening added to justify the renderer's ball-on-seat choice in FIGS. 2 and 3, and must be removed from the text rather than kept; (c) a materials-selection sentence (the disclosure says nothing about materials, and it introduces the undefined, unnumbered term "the sealing elements"); (d) structural variants of the spring-biased detent ("a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger") and of the flexible lip ("formed integrally ... or as a separate resilient element"). None of these appears anywhere in the inventor's words.

SCOPE. The disclosure says the window "shows one of three reference numerals carried on the collar." The draft renames these throughout to "dose setting indicia," a genus broader than the disclosed species, and carries the broadened term into claims 9 and 19. Reported as a major claim_scope finding with a text-only fix; the FIG. 4 plain-patch depiction may stand as a schematic convention once the text says "numerals."

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (5 findings). FIG. 3 has two flow-path defects. First, the flush poppet is placed at the closed left (supply) end of the annular rinse channel, not at the flush bypass, contradicting the description and claims 1 and 13 ("a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"); and its stem geometry is self-contradictory — the pin is "left of the inner wall," the stem's driven end is under the pin, the stem "runs leftward to a conical head," yet the head is said to sit at a seat in the transverse boss, which lies to the right of the pin. Second, FIG. 3 assigns the lower half and the upper half of one and the same annulus two different identities and two different flows ("The clear gap between the lower bands is the annular rinse channel ... The gap between the upper bands is an open passage carrying liquid to the right"), and then has the flush bypass discharge into that same annulus, so the rinse stream recirculates instead of reaching the outlet. FIG. 4 is described in 07-drawings.md as having "a portion of the housing wall broken away," but the FIG. 4 brief contains no housing wall and no break line; it instead floats an unnumbered bracket that "does not touch the collar." FIG. 4 also spaces the three detent recesses along the collar's upper silhouette and the three indicia along the visible surface — i.e., axially — although both sets are selected by rotation of the collar, so an axially spaced set cannot be indexed by "one increment" of turn and cannot present one indicium at a time to the window. Two minor items: FIG. 1 renders the inlet and outlet as downward radial stubs on the same side of the housing, in tension with "an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end" (claim 12); and FIG. 2 omits the housing wall and annular gap that FIGS. 1 and 3 show over the same region, running the admission-port tube off-sheet as though carrier liquid were supplied externally rather than from inlet 14.

One further minor fidelity item: the description calls the carrier-liquid admission port "a radial port," a term the disclosure applies only to the concentrate port and the rinse openings.

Total: 12 findings — 4 critical, 5 major, 3 minor. Each carries a filing-clean fix that is text- or brief-side only; no fix adds a speculative shape or optional embodiment.

findings.title: Unsupported actuator variants for the piston rod
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "A piston 28 is axially slidable..." (sentence on piston rod 36)
findings.detail: The description asserts an external actuating member and names three alternative actuation sources. The disclosure never states how the piston is driven; it refers only to strokes of the piston and to the piston rod as the carrier of the follower pin. There is no affirmative USER passage naming a hand lever, a pneumatic actuator, a hydraulic actuator, or any other source of reciprocating motion.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke by an external actuating member, whether a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by a follower pin carried by the piston rod. Each full piston stroke turns the index collar by one increment." — the source names the rod and the stroke but no actuating member.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke."

findings.title: Unsupported "any form ... such as" broadening of the one-way outlet valve
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "A piston 28 is axially slidable..." (final sentence)
findings.detail: The description adds an open-ended genus and three species for the one-way outlet valve. The disclosure names the element only functionally. This sentence also operates as an application-text statement added to license the renderer's ball-on-conical-seat choice in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 briefs, which the preflight forbids: the depiction convention must stay confined to the figure brief and must not be justified by broadening the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The one-way outlet valve 38 may take any form that passes liquid in one direction only, such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve into the main flow." No affirmative passage describes any structure of that valve.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full. Leave the FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 briefs unchanged, since each already labels the ball and seat "shown schematically" and the claims and description remain shape-neutral as to the one-way outlet valve.

findings.title: Unsupported materials statement, and an undefined "sealing elements"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The materials of the metering sleeve 18..." (first sentence)
findings.detail: The description asserts a material-selection criterion. The disclosure contains no statement about materials, compatibility, or chemical resistance anywhere. The sentence also introduces "the sealing elements" as a part, with no numeral, no antecedent, and no source support.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The materials of the metering sleeve 18, the piston 28, the flexible lip 56 and the sealing elements are selected for compatibility with the carrier liquid and with the concentrate to be dosed." Nearest source (disclosure.md): "The concentrate may be aggressive..." — this phrase does not appear in the disclosure at all; the disclosure's closest content is "A reusable inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable dose of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid," which says nothing about materials. No affirmative passage exists.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full.

findings.title: Unsupported structural variants of the spring-biased detent and the flexible lip
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The materials of the metering sleeve 18..." (second sentence)
findings.detail: The description offers a ball/plunger alternative for the detent and an integral/separate alternative for the flexible lip. The disclosure names both parts functionally only. Neither alternative is disclosed, and the detent alternative also serves to license the ball depicted in the FIG. 4 brief, which the preflight forbids the application text from doing.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The spring-biased detent 48 may be a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger, and the flexible lip 56 may be formed integrally with the upstream sealing land 30 or as a separate resilient element retained on it." Nearest sources (disclosure.md): "A spring-biased detent engages one of three recesses to retain the selected setting." and "a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land first wipes the dose-chamber wall." No affirmative passage describes the internal form of either part.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence in full (this removes the whole paragraph together with the preceding materials sentence). Leave the FIG. 4 detent depiction unchanged; it is already labeled "shown schematically" and, once this sentence is removed, the description and claims are shape-neutral as to the detent.

findings.title: Disclosed "reference numerals" broadened to "dose setting indicia" in the claims and throughout
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claims 9 and 19; draft/06-summary.md final indexing paragraph; draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraphs on FIG. 4 and the "In use" recap; draft/numerals.md entry 54; figures/fig-04.md
findings.detail: The disclosure supports a display of numerals. The draft substitutes the genus "indicia," which also reads on symbols, colours, bars or blank marks that the inventor never described, and carries that genus into two claims. No affirmative USER passage supports any non-numeral marking.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 9): "further comprising a transparent window in the housing and three dose setting indicia carried by the index collar"; candidate (claim 19): "displaying, through a transparent window in the housing, one of three dose setting indicia carried by the index collar". Source (disclosure.md): "A transparent window in the housing shows one of three reference numerals carried on the collar, so the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics."
findings.fix: Replace "dose setting indicia" with "dose setting numerals" and "dose setting indicium" with "dose setting numeral" in claims 9 and 19, in draft/06-summary.md, in draft/08-detailed-description.md, in draft/numerals.md (numeral 54: "dose setting numerals"), and in figures/fig-04.md. The FIG. 4 plain-patch rendering may remain as a schematic convention confined to the figure brief.

findings.title: FIG. 3 places the flush poppet at the closed supply end of the rinse channel, and its stem geometry is impossible
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md, geometry bullets 2 and 5, versus draft/08-detailed-description.md and draft/09-claims.md claims 1 and 13
findings.detail: Two verified defects in one element. (1) The brief seats the poppet in a boss that closes the left end of the annular rinse channel — i.e. it gates the carrier-liquid supply — while the description and both independent claims recite a flush poppet connected to the flush bypass, which the same brief locates at the far right of the view. (2) The stem cannot reach the stated seat: the pin is left of the inner wall, hence left of the boss; the stem's driven end is under the pin; the stem then "runs leftward" to the head, placing the head further left still, yet the seat is said to be in the boss to the right.
findings.evidence: Brief: "The clear gap between the lower bands is the annular rinse channel, closed at the left by a hatched transverse boss." / "A short pin projects downward from the shaft left of the inner wall, its lower end bearing on the right end of a stem that runs leftward to a conical head. The head stands clear of a seat in an opening through the transverse boss..." / "Right of that ball, a further opening through the upper inner band joins the bore to the upper passage: the flush bypass." Text: "The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26." Claim 1: "a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass".
findings.fix: Amend figures/fig-03.md: delete the transverse boss at the left end of the annular gap and leave that end open to the inlet; seat the conical head of the flush poppet in the flush-bypass opening through the upper inner band at the right, held open clear of that seat; and draw the stem running rightward from beneath the follower pin, along the annular space above the inner wall, to that head, so the pin bears on the left end of the stem near the end of the return stroke. Update the target for 58 to read: "the conical head clear of its seat in the flush-bypass opening at the right."

findings.title: FIG. 3 splits one annulus into two differently identified passages and returns the rinse flow into it
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md, geometry bullets 2 and 7, versus draft/09-claims.md claim 1 and draft/08-detailed-description.md
findings.detail: In a longitudinal section the upper and lower gaps between the sleeve and the housing are the two cut halves of a single annulus. The brief gives them different identities and different flows, which asserts an undisclosed divided annulus, and it then has the flush bypass discharge into the upper half of that same annulus, so the rinse stream re-enters its own supply instead of travelling to the outlet. The claims and description recite one undivided "annular rinse channel between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing."
findings.evidence: Brief: "The clear gap between the lower bands is the annular rinse channel... The gap between the upper bands is an open passage carrying liquid to the right." and "Right of that ball, a further opening through the upper inner band joins the bore to the upper passage: the flush bypass." Claim 1: "an annular rinse channel between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing". Source (disclosure.md): "Carrier liquid flows through an annular rinse channel between the sleeve and housing, through two radial rinse openings ... and then through the flush bypass to the outlet."
findings.fix: Amend figures/fig-03.md so that the upper and lower gaps between the inner wall and the outer wall are one annular rinse channel over the same axial extent; close that annulus at its right-hand end with a hatched transverse boss; and draw the flush bypass as an opening through the inner band that passes to the right of that boss into the housing interior leading to the outlet. Restate the target for 60 as "the clear gap between the lower bands, left of the rinse openings, being the lower half of the annular rinse channel."

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief has no broken-away housing wall, contrary to the Brief Description of the Drawings
findings.where: draft/07-drawings.md FIG. 4 entry versus figures/fig-04.md
findings.detail: The Brief Description states that a portion of the housing wall is broken away in FIG. 4. The FIG. 4 brief contains no housing wall, no break line, and no hatching for a housing; it shows only the collar, an unnumbered tube, the rod, the pin, the stop faces, the notches, the detent and the indicia. The detent's spring is instead carried by an unnumbered bracket that touches nothing.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 4 is a fragmentary side view of the index collar and the parts that set and retain the dose, with a portion of the housing wall broken away." figures/fig-04.md: "Above the collar, a spring-biased detent is shown schematically as a small ball resting in the middle notch, a short coil spring above the ball, and a small open bracket above the spring carrying it; the bracket does not touch the collar." No housing appears anywhere in the FIG. 4 brief.
findings.fix: In draft/07-drawings.md, change the FIG. 4 entry to: "FIG. 4 is a fragmentary side view of the index collar and the parts that set and retain the dose." Leave the schematic bracket in figures/fig-04.md, which is confined to the brief and adds no numbered structure.

findings.title: FIG. 4 spaces the detent recesses and the dose setting marks axially, although both are selected by rotation
findings.where: figures/fig-04.md, geometry bullets 5 and 7, versus draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraphs on the index collar and the window
findings.detail: The collar turns by one increment per full stroke and does not translate. Notches spaced along the collar's upper silhouette and marks spaced along the visible surface are axially spaced, so rotation would never bring a different notch under the detent, and all three marks would lie on the same generatrix and be presented to the window together. The text requires one recess engaged and one mark displayed per rotational increment.
findings.evidence: Brief: "Three shallow notches are spaced along the upper outline of the collar body, each a small rounded recess in that outline." and "Three small plain rectangular patches are spaced apart along the lower part of the visible cylindrical surface." Text: "Each full stroke of the piston draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment"; "The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting indicia 54 carried by the index collar 40." Source (disclosure.md): "A spring-biased detent engages one of three recesses to retain the selected setting. A transparent window in the housing shows one of three reference numerals carried on the collar."
findings.fix: Amend figures/fig-04.md so that the three detent recesses lie at one axial station and at three angular positions about the collar, drawn as one rounded notch broken into the upper outline with the other two shown in broken line on the curved surface to either side of it; and so that the three dose setting marks likewise lie at one axial station at three angular positions, with the middle one full on the visible surface and the outer two running off toward the silhouettes. Update targets 50 and 54 to name "the notch broken into the upper outline" and "the patch full on the visible surface" respectively.

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows radial side stubs where the text recites end connections
findings.where: figures/fig-01.md, geometry bullet 3, versus draft/08-detailed-description.md first FIG. 1 paragraph and draft/09-claims.md claim 12
findings.detail: Both the inlet and the outlet are drawn as stubs projecting downward from the same lower housing wall band, near but not at the axial ends. The description and claim 12 recite the inlet at one axial end and the outlet at the opposite axial end, following the disclosure. The figure should place the connections at the extreme ends so it illustrates the recited relationship.
findings.evidence: Brief: "A short tubular stub projects downward from the lower housing wall band near the left end and opens into the interior; it is the inlet, shown schematically. A second such stub projects downward near the right end; it is the outlet, shown schematically." Claim 12: "the inlet being at one axial end of the housing and the outlet being at an opposite axial end of the housing." Source (disclosure.md): "The valve has a cylindrical housing with an inlet at one axial end and an outlet at the opposite axial end."
findings.fix: Amend the bullet to read: "A short tubular stub opens through the lower housing wall band at the extreme left-hand end of the housing, immediately inboard of the end cap, and opens into the interior; it is the inlet, shown schematically. A second such stub opens through the lower wall band at the extreme right-hand end, immediately inboard of the end wall; it is the outlet, shown schematically. Both stubs end clear of the drawing area boundary."

findings.title: FIG. 2 omits the housing and annular gap shown for the same region in FIGS. 1 and 3
findings.where: figures/fig-02.md, geometry bullets 1, 5 and 6, versus figures/fig-01.md and figures/fig-03.md
findings.detail: FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 are both enlargements of the metering portion of FIG. 1, but FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve alone with no surrounding housing wall and no annular gap, and runs the carrier-liquid admission tube off the sheet as though carrier liquid were supplied from outside the valve. The description states that carrier liquid reaches the valve only at inlet 14 and passes along the housing.
findings.evidence: figures/fig-02.md: "The metering sleeve is cut lengthwise on its axis and appears as an upper hatched wall band and a lower hatched wall band running across the width of the drawing area." and "A short tube continues downward from it and ends clear of the drawing area boundary. This opening is the carrier-liquid admission port..." figures/fig-03.md, same region: "An outer wall cut lengthwise appears as upper and lower hatched bands along the top and bottom of the drawing area. Inside it, an inner tubular wall appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward from the outer bands..." Text: "Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16."
findings.fix: Amend figures/fig-02.md to add, above the upper sleeve band and below the lower sleeve band, a hatched housing wall band spaced outward from the sleeve with a clear gap between, matching FIG. 3; carry the concentrate tube upward through the upper housing band to end clear of the drawing area; and terminate the carrier-liquid admission opening at the clear gap below the sleeve instead of at a tube leaving the sheet.

findings.title: "Radial" applied to the carrier-liquid admission port without source support
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical."
findings.detail: The disclosure applies "radial" to the concentrate port and to the two rinse openings, but not to the carrier-liquid admission port, which it names without any orientation. The draft tracks the source term faithfully elsewhere, so the added attribute here is an untraced structural specification.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The carrier-liquid admission port 24 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20." Source (disclosure.md): "The sleeve defines a cylindrical dose chamber, a radial concentrate port, a carrier-liquid admission port, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber."
findings.fix: Change the sentence to: "The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20." Correspondingly, in figures/fig-02.md change "A second radial opening passes through the lower wall band" to "A second opening passes through the lower wall band."
